Smoothing Rough, Bumpy Texture
The Keratosis Pilaris Treatment
Keratosis pilaris, sometimes called "chicken skin," is a common, benign, non-contagious condition causing patches of rough-feeling bumps — typically on the upper arms, thighs, cheeks, and buttocks — where keratin clogs and blocks the opening of hair follicles.

The bumps can resemble goosebumps or plucked-chicken skin, often with slight pinkness, itchiness, or a sandpaper-like feel, and vary in colour depending on skin tone. ISAAC Luxe addresses the condition through chemical peels, fractional CO2 laser, and topical ointments, selected according to severity and skin type.

Treatment Options

Chemical Peels

Exfoliate clogged follicles and smooth rough texture.

Fractional CO2 Laser

Resurfaces affected areas for a smoother, more even texture.

Topical Ointments

Dermatologist-guided creams to manage keratin build-up.

What It Treats
Rough, Bumpy Texture Upper Arms & Thighs Redness Around Bumps Dry, Irritated Skin
